# Surface and Mesh Extraction

Also called: Gaussian Mesh Extraction, 3DGS Surface Reconstruction

## Overview
This family provides methods to derive explicit geometric representations (meshes, point clouds, or semantic segmentations) from trained 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) models. Standard 3DGS renders implicit volumetric fields; these extensions bridge the gap to explicit geometry for applications requiring mesh-based editing, simulation, or semantic understanding. They differ from sibling methods by their specific geometric priors: [Gaussian Opacity Fields (GOF) Mesh Extraction](3692-gaussian-opacity-fields-gof-mesh-extraction.md) treats opacity as a continuous density field for isosurface extraction; [Distance-based Gaussian Splatting](7411-distance-based-gaussian-splatting.md) enforces alignment with a pre-existing mesh; [2D-Lift-3D Scene Segmentation](11513-2d-lift-3d-scene-segmentation.md) lifts 2D semantic masks to 3D primitives; and [Mesh Extraction via Poisson Reconstruction](12790-mesh-extraction-via-poisson-reconstruction.md) converts rendered depth/normal maps into an oriented point cloud for volumetric reconstruction.

## Shared principles
All methods operate on the output of a trained 3DGS model $\mathcal{G} = \{G_i\}_{i=1}^M$. They rely on the standard geometric projection where 3D Gaussians are transformed into ray space. The projected 2D covariance $\mathbf{\hat{\Sigma}}_i$ is computed using the Jacobian $J$ of the affine approximation of the projection and the rotation part $W$ of the extrinsic matrix:
$$ \mathbf{\hat{\Sigma}}_i = J W \mathbf{\Sigma}_i W^T J^T $$
[4971-radiative-and-tomographic-gaussians.md]

Unlike standard rendering which outputs RGB, these methods extract geometric attributes (depth, normal, distance, or semantic labels) from the Gaussian primitives or their projections. They generally do not modify the core 3DGS training objective but instead post-process the optimized parameters or use them as priors for external reconstruction algorithms.

## Subtopics

### [Gaussian Opacity Fields (GOF) Mesh Extraction](3692-gaussian-opacity-fields-gof-mesh-extraction.md)
A method to extract a 3-D triangulated mesh from a trained Gaussian model without retraining, by building a volumetric density field and extracting an isosurface. It builds on [Surface and Mesh Extraction](8498-surface-and-mesh-extraction.md) by treating the Gaussian opacity field as a continuous volumetric density function, distinct from sibling methods that rely on distance fields or direct point-cloud reconstruction.

### [Distance-based Gaussian Splatting](7411-distance-based-gaussian-splatting.md)
Distance-based Gaussian Splatting is a method for high-quality rendering and geometric refinement that establishes a bidirectional connection between a pre-existing 3D mesh $\mathcal{M}$ and a set of 3D Gaussian splats $\mathcal{G}$. It solves the problem of redundant or misaligned Gaussian primitives that typically arise when initializing splats on dense meshes or when standard densification creates geometry that deviates from the underlying surface. Unlike standard 3D Gaussian Splatting which treats all splats equally, this method classifies splats as either "tightly-bound" (aligned with the mesh surface) or "loosely-bound" (allowing for surface artifacts or fine details) based on their distance to the mesh, and masks out splats occluded by the opaque mesh surface.

### [2D-Lift-3D Scene Segmentation](11513-2d-lift-3d-scene-segmentation.md)
2D-Lift-3D Scene Segmentation is a training-free method for segmenting 3D Gaussian primitives by lifting 2D segmentation masks from a reference view into 3D space. It solves the problem of isolating specific objects or parts within a volumetric scene represented by 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) to enable partial scene editing (PSE). Unlike methods that require learnable feature vectors or explicit surface reconstruction, this approach relies on multi-view label voting to assign semantic labels to Gaussians based on 2D foundation model outputs. It is distinguished from [Gaussian Opacity Fields (GOF) Mesh Extraction](3692-gaussian-opacity-fields-gof-mesh-extraction.md) by its focus on semantic grouping for editing rather than geometric mesh extraction, and from [Distance-based Gaussian Splatting](7411-distance-based-gaussian-splatting.md) by its reliance on external 2D priors rather than implicit distance fields.

### [Mesh Extraction via Poisson Reconstruction](12790-mesh-extraction-via-poisson-reconstruction.md)
This method extracts a textured triangular mesh $\mathcal{M} = (\mathcal{V}, \mathcal{F})$ from an optimized 3D Gaussian Splatting model by converting rendered 2D depth and normal maps into a 3D oriented point cloud, which is then reconstructed using Poisson surface reconstruction. It differs from implicit field-based extraction (e.g., [Gaussian Opacity Fields (GOF) Mesh Extraction](3692-gaussian-opacity-fields-gof-mesh-extraction.md)) by operating directly on the explicit Gaussian primitives' geometric projections, and from distance-based methods (e.g., [Distance-based Gaussian Splatting](7411-distance-based-gaussian-splatting.md)) by relying on volumetric integration of oriented samples rather than signed distance function minimization.

## Background
The extraction of explicit geometry from 3D Gaussian Splatting is a recent development following the introduction of 3DGS [4971-radiative-and-tomographic-gaussians.md]. As 3DGS gained popularity for novel view synthesis, the need for editable, mesh-based representations for downstream tasks (CAD, simulation, AR/VR) drove the development of these extraction techniques. The methods cited here represent early attempts to bridge the gap between differentiable rasterization of Gaussians and traditional computer vision reconstruction pipelines.
